caption:
Milton movers: quote changed mid-move?

Moving into a new Milton home? Before you book movers, ask these questions: 1) Get the quote in writing, and ask what could change the final price. 2) Ask what the mover's insurance covers, and whether you may need more. 3) Book once your closing date is firm, and ask what happens if closing slips by a day. 4) Tell the movers about stairs, elevators and parking ahead of time. These are planning questions, not rules, and it can help to compare more than one quote.

Georgetown sellers: inspect before listing?

Picture this: you are getting ready to list your Georgetown home and wonder whether to order an inspection first. Questions to ask: 1) A pre-listing inspection is one you order yourself, before the home goes on the market. 2) It may show problems before buyers find them, while you still have time to decide what to do. 3) Ask your lawyer what you must disclose to buyers once you know about a problem. 4) Ask your Realtor® whether it makes sense for your home, and get quotes first. These are planning questions, not promises: your lawyer and your agreements decide the details, and no sale price or timeline is guaranteed.

A $10K card balance. Mortgage hit?

New Reel on my page tonight: how a credit card balance can count against the mortgage you qualify for, worked out step by step. Take a guess first.

Example only. Not mortgage, tax or legal advice.

Krishna Rander, Realtor® | PROPERTY.CA INC., Brokerage

#GTArealestate #mortgagetips #keyswithkrishna

$10K card. Smaller mortgage?

Example only, in Mississauga terms: you carry a $10,000 credit card balance and want to buy.
1) CMHC's debt-service guideline counts revolving credit at no less than 3% of the balance per month: 3% x $10,000 = $300 a month counted as debt.
2) Lenders test your mortgage at the greater of your rate + 2% or 5.25%. With an example rate of 4.34%, that is 6.34%.
3) At 6.34% over 25 years (interest compounded semi-annually), $300 a month supports a mortgage of about $45,444. If your debt ratio is already at its limit, that is roughly the mortgage room the card could use up. Paying the balance down before you apply may free it, so ask your lender how they count your debts.
Lenders set their own rules and ratios. 4.34% is an example from the lowest advertised 5-year fixed rates (insured); your rate will differ.

caption:
All six banks: Dec. 9 hike?

Bloomberg reported on November 26, 2026 that all six of Canada's biggest banks now expect the Bank of Canada to raise its rate at the December 9 decision. BMO and CIBC moved their forecasts from January to December earlier this week, and TD was the last to switch. The Bank's rate is 2.5% after its October hike, the first increase in three years, and traders in overnight swaps put the odds of a December hike at about 80% as of November 25 (Bloomberg). Global News reported (November 25-26) that CIBC's Avery Shenfeld said December "might be where the rate hikes stop," while BMO's Sal Guatieri cautioned a hike "could end up being premature" if the economy softens.
What it could mean: variable-rate borrowers could see a change in their rate or in how much of their payment goes to interest, while fixed rates follow bond yields. Example per $1,000,000 borrowed: at an example 4.34% (25-year amortization, interest compounded semi-annually), the monthly mortgage is about $5,446; at 4.59% (a quarter point higher) it is about $5,585, roughly $139 more. Calculations by Krishna Rander's team. Forecasts can change, and these are the banks' and traders' expectations, not a forecast from me.
Raise, hold or cut? Comment your guess.

Oakville home. Windows fogged?

Quick tip: on your next Oakville showing, check for fog or moisture between the window panes and ask how old the windows are. Fog between the panes may mean a seal has failed, so ask your inspector to take a look and your Realtor® how it could factor into your offer. This is a question to ask, not a rule: every home is different.
